title: Local authority foundation validation
scope: Checkout authority model, graph assembly, JVM contract suite and experimental two-ABI Android package build. This does not validate Android authority enrollment, sign-in, Keystore persistence or business-command enforcement because those paths are not implemented.

checks.name: complete checkout JVM model suite
checks.result: passed with -Werror and jvm-target 1.8; includes CheckoutAuthorityTest plus every pre-existing checkout model test

checks.name: experimental checkout Android package
checks.command: OPENBMT_GUARD=<temporary direct coordinator runner> CHECKOUTAPK_OUT=/tmp/openbmt-checkout-apk CHECKOUTAPK_KEYDIR=/tmp/openbmt-checkout-keys CHECKOUTAPK_CARGO_TARGET=/tmp/openbmt-checkout-cargo apps/checkout-android/build.sh
checks.result: passed; Rust native libraries built for arm64-v8a and x86_64, Kotlin compiled with -Werror, APK dexed, aligned and test-signed

artifact.signature: apksigner verification passed with one test signer using APK Signature Scheme v3

open_gates: No Android CheckoutAuthorityStorage implementation with Keystore-backed authenticated sealing is wired.
No first-manager enrollment, recovery acknowledgement, staff sign-in or lifecycle lock UI is wired.
No sale, tender, cash, refund, catalog, inventory, report or integration command calls CheckoutAuthority.
No actor attribution is persisted in business journals and no authority-admin audit log exists.
The local recovery bearer code is not Owner-app approval and is not exposed as a completed recovery workflow.
No emulator or physical-device authority workflow was run.
claim_boundary: The evidence supports a compiled and tested reusable model foundation only. Canonical capability statuses and benchmark parity remain unchanged.
